### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via remoteColumn (literal, a string literal in aggregate))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class), applyTenantScope (literal, a string literal in aggregate))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via EngineAggregateOptionsSchema (symbol, a top-level const), IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via generateSql (symbol, a method of class ObjectQLStrategy))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLStrategy (symbol, a top-level class), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 144cdc254e44ecd77f9d011714afaefdb2eecc32` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b4bcee2bf151868c14aed89298cd35f3bfd04312` — the merge of head `f9fa972988f4479ec681d3d56650ff957d73a428` into base `144cdc254e44ecd77f9d011714afaefdb2eecc32`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b4bcee2bf151868c14aed89298cd35f3bfd04312 && git checkout b4bcee2bf151868c14aed89298cd35f3bfd04312
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 144cdc254e44ecd77f9d011714afaefdb2eecc32 f9fa972988f4479ec681d3d56650ff957d73a428 && git checkout -B drift-repro 144cdc254e44ecd77f9d011714afaefdb2eecc32 && git merge --no-ff f9fa972988f4479ec681d3d56650ff957d73a428

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 144cdc254e44ecd77f9d011714afaefdb2eecc32
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 144cdc254e44ecd77f9d011714afaefdb2eecc32` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · REWORK (1 item)** · head `03414032f18a089c3b5759f627724f9511d36b22` · card #33697 · read 2026-11-17T00:14Z

Code read in parallel with CI, as the seat asked. At the reading this head had 13 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 22 `in_progress` and 1 `failure`: `Check Changeset`, which is item 1 below.

### REWORK

1. **`Metadata-protocol: none` is wrong for this diff; the changeset level follows it.** `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/DriverCapabilities:zonedDateBucketing`, a new authorable key, and AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3) reads a new key as `added`, which takes at least `minor` on the package that carries it. `Check Changeset` (job 133712448234) refuses this head for exactly that: "it moves a metadata-protocol baseline the ratchets record … Declare `Metadata-protocol: added` … and grade the package at least `minor`". The sibling bit had the same shape: `aggregationFilter` (#33698, `.changeset/33698-measure-filter-pushdown.md`) shipped `@objectstack/spec: minor` with a non-`none` kind. Fix, in one commit:
   - PR body and changeset body: `Metadata-protocol: added` (keep `Clause-②: yes (widening)`).
   - `.changeset/33697-pg-zoned-date-bucketing.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`.
   - PR body: the third line a non-`none` kind owes, `Skills-docs: updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON`. This is not a `domain:skills` PR, so `updated here` is not available; the area picks between `follow-up #N` and `none — REASON` (for example, if no skill teaches driver capability bits), and the seat files the card if it is a follow-up.
   - ⛔ No baseline edit to quiet the gate; the shard is right as generated.

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, attribution header then `Fixes #33697`. Closing-keyword scan of the whole body: one hit, `#33697` (PR #33774 is named without a keyword).
- **File surface:** 25 files from `get_files`. All inside claim 6931083810 plus amendment 6933427092 (the extra driver-sql helpers, `driver.zod.ts` and `driver.test.ts`, the three service-analytics files), the generated spec artefacts (`api-surface/contracts.json`, `export-origins/contracts.json`, `authorable-surface/data.json`) and the three generated `content/docs/references/data/driver*.mdx` rows. No `content/docs/releases/`, no unrelated file. Merge commit `f24d2262` brings `main` in; the three-dot diff holds only these 25.
- **Contract read (for the L1 side; the L2 judges it):** `DriverAggregateQuery` is kept off `DriverQuery`, so `find()` / `count()` gain no key they would drop. The bit is ANDed with method presence in the engine (`zoneNative` reads `drv?.supports?.zonedDateBucketing === true`; ablation A3). The raw request string never reaches a driver: `withBucketZone` sends only `judgeBucketZone`'s resolved area name.
- **Driver read:** the zone is a bound value (`AT TIME ZONE ?`, bindings `[field, timezone]`); a `Field.date` keeps its calendar-day arm; every non-PostgreSQL dialect answers `null` for a zone. The GROUP BY names the select position when zoned (`groupByRaw(String(selectPosition))`); ablation A1 records PostgreSQL's 42803 when the expression is spelled twice. A direct `aggregate()` with a zone is judged before compiling: 501 on a dialect without the bit, 400 on a zone that is not its own resolved area name.
- **Behaviour moves that were in-memory before:** `Etc/UTC`, `GMT`, `Zulu`, and any spelling that resolves to `UTC`, now take the native UTC path (ablation A4). Same buckets by construction; the enumeration pin moves them to the UTC class and says why.
- **Rejection assertions:** the zoned matrix refuses `CST`, `US/Eastern`, `+08:00`, `EST5EDT`, `Bogus/Zone` and the SQLite dialect case with `code` and `status` (`sql-driver-33697-zoned-date-bucket.test.ts:130-131`, `:205-206`); the engine describe pins each spelling's dispatch.
- **Tests and controls:** four ablations, each with what went red (A1 26, A2 16, A3 5, A4 3), plus a fixture-sensitivity pin keeping the parity non-vacuous. Live PostgreSQL 16 cell run locally (server `Asia/Shanghai`, process `TZ=America/New_York`). The three forced test changes are named in the body with the ruling they follow.
- **Changeset and docs sentences, checked against the diff:** "SQLite (no tz database), MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle keep the in-memory path" (`zonedDateBucketing: this.isPostgres`; `buildDateBucketExpr` returns `null` for a zone off PostgreSQL); "refused `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`/501 … `INVALID_QUERY`/400" (`refuseZonedDateBucket(…, 'dialect' | 'unresolved', …)` in `aggregate`); "`CST` resolves to `America/Chicago`" (`judgeBucketZone`); the generated `driver*.mdx` rows carry the schema's `.describe()` string verbatim. Only the level and the kind in the changeset are wrong (item 1).
- **Landing tier:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34530`: 0 of 25 paths governed, 967 changed lines (+860 / −107) ≤ 3000 ⇒ ordinary queue landing by the area after L1 ACCEPT and L2 PASS on the same green head.

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts` are non-test `packages/spec/src/**`, plus `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The area reports it already sent to the review seat; the record has to name the head that lands, and item 1 moves the head.

### Out of scope, for the area to place before ACCEPT (one line each: `filed #N` or `dropped — reason`)

- Acceptance note 1: SQLite fixed-offset pushdown (the amendment's optional arm) not taken; "a follow-up card can measure it".
- Acceptance note 2: the zone-resolution rule is written three times (`judgeBucketZone` in objectql, `resolvedAreaZone` in driver-sql, `echoBucketZone` in service-analytics); the body names `@objectstack/core` as its home, outside this card's surface. The engine and the echo are held together by the enumeration pin; the driver copy is not.

### Next

L1 reads the delta only, on a head whose CI is green and announced final in a PR comment.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03414032f18a089c3b5759f627724f9511d36b22`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-date-bucket.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-class-head.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/types.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts

Inputs read: card #33697 body and all 8 comments; PR #34530 body and file list (25 files); the net diff against main (merge base bdd51769, equal to origin/main); the check-runs on the head; ADR-0053 Phase 2 D2 with its amendment note on main; the gate source scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and the Temporal Conformance job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, read only.

Check-runs on the head (45): `Check Changeset` concluded FAILURE. Success: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint scoped tooling self-tests, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Check PR Size, Auto Label, filter, the two shard planners, Dogfood Regression Gate. Skipped: Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, the queue verdicts, the opt-in harnesses. PENDING (in progress when read, no verdict): Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, every Type Check job, Lint ESLint, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint docs and code guards, both remaining scoped lints.

### ① Derived judgments

- New public type `DriverAggregateQuery` (a `DriverQuery` plus optional `timezone`) exported from `@objectstack/spec/contracts`; api-surface and export-origins carry it. Right: additive, one export added, none removed.
- `IDataDriver.aggregate` second parameter moves from `DriverQuery` to `DriverAggregateQuery`. Right as a widening: the new type is a subtype of the old, so an existing implementer declared with `DriverQuery` stays assignable and an existing caller passing a `DriverQuery` still compiles. The type-level proof is the Type Check jobs, PENDING on this head.
- New accepted key `supports.zonedDateBucketing` (optional boolean) on `DriverCapabilitiesSchema`; the accept set widens by one key, the non-boolean value is refused, absence means false. Right, and it arrives with its engine reader in the same change, the bar the schema docblock and the amendment set for a new bit.
- The authorable-surface baseline moves: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/DriverCapabilities:zonedDateBucketing`. This is a key added to what an author can write. The PR declares `Metadata-protocol: none` over it. WRONG, see M1 in ②.
- `EngineAggregateOptions.timezone`: schema unchanged (free string, optional), jsdoc only. Right. The dispatch behind it changes with no change to the answer contract: a name the runtime resolves to UTC now takes the native path (it took the in-memory path, same buckets), and an area/location zone goes to a declaring driver.
- driver-sql `aggregate()` now refuses two inputs it used to answer as a UTC bucket: a zoned call on a dialect without the bit (501) and a zone string that is not its own resolved area/location name on PostgreSQL (400). Right: no engine path sent a `timezone` key to a driver before this change (the engine builds the AST key by key and never copied it), so no served request is narrowed; the refusal replaces a silent wrong answer for a direct caller only.
- `dateBucketSql` gains an optional fourth argument on `SqlDriver`, the analytics plugin bridge, `DatasetScopedStrategyContext` and `AnalyticsServiceConfig`. Right: additive, not an `IDataDriver` member.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the declaration is right as to the arm: one optional capability key and one exported type are added, nothing is narrowed at any published accept set.

M1 (must-fix) — the level and the `Metadata-protocol:` line do not match what the diff publishes. The changeset and the PR body both declare `Metadata-protocol: none` and grade every package `patch`, while the diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` (a new key). AGENTS.md states a new key is `added` and that a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states that a declared `none` may not move an `authorable-surface/` baseline. The check-run `Check Changeset` on this head concluded FAILURE, which is that gate's verdict; I name the cause from the gate's written rule and the diff, the job log was not read. Precedent on main for the same shape: `.changeset/33698-measure-filter-pushdown.md` (the `aggregationFilter` bit) declares a kind and grades `@objectstack/spec` minor. Fix: `Metadata-protocol: added` in the changeset body and the PR body, and `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. The dev report's "128 derived gates, all exit 0" does not cover this: that axis is PR-scoped and has no input in a local run.

The package list is otherwise right: spec, objectql, driver-sql and service-analytics are the packages whose published source moves; driver-turso is not moved.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (public names): answered, option A, keep `zonedDateBucketing` and `DriverAggregateQuery`. The bit name sits beside `aggregationFilter` and says what the driver does; the separate type is the sounder carrier, because `find()` and `count()` take `DriverQuery` and would declare a key they drop. `DriverOptions.timezone` is rightly left alone, it is the execution-context zone.
- open_questions 2 (route to contract review): answered by this record.
- Deviation, widened file surface: covered by the claim amendment 6933427092; every added file is in the claimed packages and no governed path is in the diff (Governed Surface Queue Guard: success).
- Deviation, check-platform-checklist not run: accepted, one export added and none renamed or removed.
- Review items (a) to (e) from the card: (a) held, see ④; (b) answered by not taking the optional SQLite arm, which the amendment permits ("may"); (c) held on all four named places; (d) held, both the engine and the echo compare the resolved name; (e) pinned in the new matrix and the engine dispatch test by the PR's account, test files being the lane's ACCEPT.
- SQL push-down (standing check): no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The change moves work into SQL. The read scope and the tenant wall are untouched: both `drv.aggregate` call sites pass the same composed AST and the same `aggregateOptions` as before, and the zone is the only added key.
- Security: the zone reaches the statement as a bound value in `aggregate()`; the raw request string never reaches a driver. `security_findings: none` is consistent with what I read.
- out_of_scope finding, the resolution rule stated three times (engine, driver, echo): accepted as a deviation for this card; it has no carrier and should get a follow-up card, since only the engine and the echo are pinned together.
- Card line "Before/after on the M0 bench": the PR carries no bench reading on this head; the figures in the card body are the M0 measurement. For the lane seat's ACCEPT, not graded here.

S1 (should-fix) — the live PostgreSQL parity reading is owed on the landing head before landing. Asked explicitly by the lane. The evidence on the head is not enough for the contract by itself:
  - What CI ran or will run on the head touches no PostgreSQL server. The Temporal Conformance job is skipped on every pull_request and merge_group event by its own condition, so the skip is by design, not a fault; it runs on push to main, on schedule and on workflow_dispatch. The PostgreSQL cells of the new matrix and the live analytics cell are opt-in on `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` and skip in Test Core. So the pins that do run in PR CI are the SQLite cells (no bit, 501, UTC served), the engine dispatch pins against a stub driver, and string pins of the rendered expression. None executes the zoned statement.
  - The two facts the contract rests on are exactly the ones only a live server answers: that PostgreSQL accepts the zone as an untyped bound parameter in `AT TIME ZONE` with the bucket grouped by select-list position, and that its labels equal `bucketDateKey` across both Berlin DST changes, Taipei, and a `Field.date` under New_York. The amendment makes that parity the acceptance rule, "a test that fails".
  - The dev's local reading (PostgreSQL 16.15, server Asia/Shanghai, process America/New_York, 61 passed and 1 skipped, ablations A1 and A2 red) is the same environment the skipped job provisions, and by reading the SQL I find no reason to doubt it: the expression is the existing UTC arm with the zone in place of the literal, and ordinal GROUP BY is valid there. But it is a dev self-report, and the first witnessed execution would otherwise be the push run on main, where a red is a main red.
  - Reading owed: one witnessed run on the landing head of what the skipped job would have run, namely the driver-sql suite and the service-analytics suite with `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` set against PostgreSQL 16 at Asia/Shanghai with `TZ=America/New_York`. Either a workflow_dispatch of ci.yml on the branch (the job's condition admits it) or the seat's own run, with the command and the counts recorded on the card, naming the head. It needs no code change; the delta record closes it on that reading.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts — holds against the amendment and its first consumer.
- "The engine sets it only on a driver that declares the bit": true. `withBucketZone` adds the key only for kind `area`, and both call sites sit under `nativeAggregate`, which requires `typeof drv.aggregate === 'function'` and `!tzRequiresInMemory`; with kind `area` that is true only when `supports.zonedDateBucketing === true`. The relation-group-join statement takes the same wrapper.
- "only the resolved name, never the raw string, never UTC": true. `judgeBucketZone` returns the `resolvedOptions().timeZone` value, maps a resolved `UTC` to the native path with no key, and the aggregate AST is built key by key, so the request's own `timezone` cannot ride it.
- "refuses a zone it cannot bucket rather than reading it as UTC": true for driver-sql, judged before anything compiles.
- The aggregate jsdoc sentence that replaced "a driver never sees it" agrees with the engine fork.

packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts — holds. Each sentence of the new docblock was checked against the code: resolve first; UTC takes the UTC path; an area/location name goes down with the resolved name when the bit is true and the method exists; every other case stays in `applyInMemoryAggregation`; `Field.date` is never zone-shifted (`calendarDay` wins over the zone in the PostgreSQL arm); the zone is a bound value; `SqlDriver` declares it as `this.isPostgres`, so SQLite, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle and TursoDriver read false. The "why a bit" paragraph matches the amendment's own reason.

packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts — holds. The rewritten `timezone` jsdoc states the three-way reading the engine implements and the amendment's test (throws or no `/` stays in memory; otherwise push down the resolved name).

Attempts to break the design, each read in the head tree:
- Review item (a), one binding: the zoned bucket is selected once and grouped by `selectPosition`. The counter increments exactly for the items that add a select column, in the same loop, before any aggregation or relation-join column is selected, and `getBuilder` pre-selects nothing, so the ordinal is the bucket's column also after a plain key, with an alias equal to the field name, with two buckets, and in the relation-join statement. The ordinal arm is reachable on PostgreSQL only, since every other dialect refuses a zone first. No ORDER BY or second spelling of the bucket exists in this door.
- Cast direction: `(col)::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE ?` is the amendment's rule verbatim, with the cast.
- Engine and driver disagreeing on a name: both resolve through the same runtime in the same process and resolution is idempotent, so a name the engine sends always passes the driver's own check. A runtime that canonicalises differently changes which of the three roads a spelling takes, not the buckets: each road answers the zone's own calendar.

The printed statement renders the zone as an escaped literal and so groups by identical text.
- Security: same AST, same options, same WHERE on both roads.
- Residual, recorded by the amendment and not a finding: a resolved name that the server's tz database lacks (two copies of tz data) is a query the database rejects rather than one bucketed in memory.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:PostgreSQL 上按非 UTC 时区(比如 Asia/Taipei、Europe/Berlin)做日、周、月、季、年分组，现在在数据库里用 `AT TIME ZONE` 分桶，不再把整批行拉进应用内存。SQLite、MySQL 等其余驱动照旧在内存分桶。驱动通过新的能力位 `supports.zonedDateBucketing` 声明自己会不会这样做。
- 为什么改：执行你的裁决「PG 在库里算，修订 ADR」(ADR-0053 D2 的修订已合)。多数用户不在 UTC,他们的日报、月报以前都走慢路径。
- 风险与回滚：只改分桶表达式，权限范围和租户墙仍在同一条 WHERE 里。库内结果和内存结果逐桶对等(PG 16 实测，含柏林两次夏令时切换)。回滚即 revert,引擎自动回到内存路径。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts`(新契约类型)、`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts`(时区只绑定一次)、`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`(按解析后的时区名分派)。
- 两分钟验证：起一个 PG(服务器时区 Asia/Shanghai),跑 `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=… pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run src/sql-driver-33697-zoned-date-bucket.test.ts`,预期 61 过、1 跳过(没配 MySQL)。
